exposure: COVID-19 pandemic period (pre-epidemic, first epidemic cohort, second epidemic cohort)
cohort: The study participants were pregnant patients who gave birth in a nonepidemic designated hospital between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2021.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a decrease in the number of births and changes in maternal-fetal outcomes, including a decrease in mean birth weight, a decrease in macrosomia and LGA, an increase in LBW and SGA, and varied changes in GDM, maternal hypertension, and neonatal asphyxia.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery underwent a marginal decrease in both the first and second epidemic cohorts compared to the pre-epidemic period.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight decreased from 3319g (pre-epidemic) to 3309g (first epidemic) and 3272g (second epidemic); outcomes also included LBW, macrosomia, LGA, and SGA.
gest_age: N/A (though preterm, SGA, LGA are related)
